Principal limitation: His example answers an infallibility requirement Clifton disavows, so evidential warrant remains 55 because Sechler’s less-than-certain posture does not address settled belief comparable to confidence in one’s spouse. Live burden: Sechler needs to explain why commitment without complete certainty resolves Clifton’s concern about nonresistant unbelief, rather than merely showing committed Christians can entertain intellectual doubt in this exchange. Locked score: The 71 remains because the distinction is lucid and relevant to practical commitment yet only partially responsive to the spouse-based standard defended in the exchange.

card.critique: Strongest feature: Clifton’s spouse analogy identifies settled everyday belief, rather than indefeasible Cartesian certainty, as the significant condition, answering Sechler and supporting responsiveness at 96. Principal limitation: Evidential warrant remains 72 because confidence that one’s wife exists illuminates the epistemic condition without demonstrating that divine love would produce comparable, anxiety-free belief among every nonresistant person. Live burden: Clifton needs to justify the analogy’s theological bridge, explaining why relationship-seeking divine love requires spouse-like doxastic security despite differences between human presence and divine self-disclosure. Locked score: The 89 remains because the reply compellingly corrects the certainty standard and advances nonresistant nonbelief, while its normative premise about what divine love must provide remains argued rather than established.
